title: Qt: Backport Welcome Screen from dev
description:
This is a backport of the welcome screen feature introduced in
!23638 to the release branch for 4.6

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude)

notes.body:
@geraldcombs this is the requested back port. I needed to change a few pieces of code as I opted for not backporting the splashoverlay and recent files list changes that are already part of 4.7. Otherwise this backport would have been much more extensive and intrusive into existing code.  

I only started both applications and played around a little, but please test this with Stratoshark and tell me if it is working.
The Welcome screen looks fine here in both Wireshark and Stratoshark on macOS. Thanks!
requested review from @geraldcombs
Move to profile independent `recent_common`.
I am working on this on the main branch. NOT on the backport. I already had to rewrite quite a few things to manage this backport and would prefer to restructure as few things as possible.
I would like this configuration to be resolved before back port to 4.6.

I need to do this in stages as the change is too massive because the code bases are too diverse already. Let me commit this. I promise you it is going to come next.

The issue here is, the more stuff I pack into this rewrite/backport the harder it will get to avoid side-effects. That is while I am trying to do it in stages. The recent_common stuff WILL be part of the upcoming 4.6

How do we justify this added feature to a stable branch when we are very strict on other changes?
And why such a hurry? Can we let it settle on the master branch before push-to-prod?

You mean settle and introduce with 5 or settle it for 4.6? I would have preferred just doing it in 5 but it was a request from the board to help with marketing and selling SharkFest.

As for 4.6, the reason I needed to push it at all was, that it is not a straight forward cherry pick. And it makes it harder and harder when both branches digress farther and farther apart. But we could revert if you'd prefer.

I'm thinking about settle regarding images, colors, what should be in code and what should be in .json, what should be configurable and how to configure it, etc. I don't have a strong opinion about adding it to 4.6.x if we agree this is a "good thing"TM.

Some examples:
* If having auto updates enabled I like the idea of having this in the sidebar even if not having the Tips or Learn section enabled.
* If having less AI "noisy" images and light-mode colors I would probably leave the Tips section enabled.
* I would like to have a simple "Version" section to show current version with bigger font than the "Version:" line we currently have on top.
* I would like to be able to reorder the sections, like having "Version" on top or bottom.
* We should have minimum section-specific code (dates, content, colors, etc), this should be configured in a .json. The `InfoBannerWidget::isAprilFoolsDay()` being one example which does not belong in code.
* The Welcome Page configuration should be extended to configure Open and Capture lists stacked or side-by-side depending on screen size. Optimal would be a 3-pane layout configuration we already know.
* A tooltip should show the URL for the buttons. This is common in browsers.
* If running a Development version we should have a Learn link to the developers guide.

Thanks for the detailed feedback! I've created issues to track these suggestions:

- #21167 — Make section content and configuration data-driven via JSON
- #21168 — Support section reordering and configurable multi-pane layout
- #21169 — Add version section and show auto-update status in sidebar
- #21170 — Show URL tooltips on buttons and add developer guide link
